column1: # The row patterns of `cells-outcome-sweep.tsv`: each distinct pattern once, with the rows
# that share it and the principle that gives it (P0-P7 and E1-E3 of S5-principles.md, the
# design's S1 (b), L1-L5 and Q1-Q3, and the S5.0 and S5.0g rulings). It is the reviewed
# judgement check 5's `SWEEP` reason names: the sweep's tuples no case covers are judged
# KRS_CELLS_PATTERNS_RECORD=1, which keeps the principle of every pattern whose answers are
# unchanged and leaves a new one's empty: the test fails until it is written.
# A pattern is exact: a table and the answers, cell by cell, of one row group across the
# table's columns (the sweep's short names and `|product:` marks).
# - readable, claim; cells; init: a row group is a side and a stack, and its pattern is its
#   rows, path `-`, `?` and `*` (init: `-` only), one line each. readable and claim have the same
#   columns, so they share patterns; a member names its forms. A row's `other` is a
#   function of its form, side and stack, so a member determines it.
# - children: a row group is one result of the sweep's children section, its pattern the
#   answers in readable, claim and cells! (whose row writes each record as its fragment); a
#   member is its stack, `other` and result, in readable's spelling.
# - children, init: a row group is one value, its pattern the one answer.
# Lines: `ID  PATH|answers  ANSWERS..` (the pattern), `ID  member  ..` (each row group that
# has it), `ID  principle  TEXT`. IDs number the patterns in the order their first member is
# The path rule, R3 (each main pattern's `?` and `*` lines): an entry naming a cell below a
#   `?` or `*` ancestor is judged on its own layers first (the form step, then P3 against the
#   cell's own stack, refusals inside its marks included) and those refusals stand; whatever
#   they admit is then refused for the ancestor (S1 (b)): `owp` below `?`, `cwi` below `*`.
#   A pairing refusal of the `-` row (rm, uor, atc, Q3's overwrite cir, F3's open record
#   over an existing group) comes after the path, so the path class replaces it. The
#   product's departures (E1 `cbi`, the List back instance `ils`, M3's readable `mrr` at the
#   kind step, M3's `cells!` `arm` at the form step) come before the path and show through.

column3: Subject on the computation: Some/None pop, braces iop, map notation mna (P3b); [x, ..] and [x] ok (P3a, P5: they constrain and bind); [..] ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint: it matches every content and binds nothing, on a cell the result leaves); [.., x] ok by the principles, the product's cbi being E1 (a [cell-exception]); [x, r @ ..] cir (Q3: a readable rule never captures the continuation; a refusal inside the mark, so it stands under a path); x, _, 0 and every record cw (P3c: a value where the computation has its mark; E2 for the whole binder). Paths: R3.

Subject on a plain Int or Set leaf: Some/None pop, every bracket spelling br (no List layer), braces iop (on the Set leaf too, ruling 4), map notation mna (P3b); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); 0 and the records sort (values: the lattice, step 4, judges a record of another sort). Paths: R3.

Subject on a List or cons leaf, alike (P2: brackets mark both): [x, ..], [x], [.., x], [x, r @ ..] ok (P3a; P6: a subject `..` matches the unwritten rest, `r @ ..` names it, and a leaf's list may be matched at either end); [..] ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); braces iop, map notation mna, Some/None pop (P3b); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry; 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: R3.

Subject on a Map leaf: { y -> x, .. } ok (P3a: the map read, its rest framed); brackets br, Some/None pop, braces of records iop (P3b; P2 reads braces of records as instances, lexically, not as map notation); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: R3.

Subject on the plain group G, which has no mark (P2): Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop, map notation mna (P3b); x ok, _ ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); 0 sort (the lattice); G { a: x, .. } and G { a: x, b: y, .. } ok (P6: a subject record's `..` leaves the other children unconstrained); G { a: x } rmc (L4: without `..` a record names every child; a kind refusal, so it stands under a path). Paths: R3.

Subject on a `?` cell over Int or G: Some(x) ok (P3a); None atc (P5: K tests absence only by creating the cell, and the result leaves it); brackets br (no List layer anywhere), braces iop, map notation mna (P3b); x, _, 0 and every record owp (P3c: a value under `?`; an incomplete record's rmc would be deeper, after the advice). Paths: R3 (atc is pairing, so the ancestor's class replaces it).

Subject on `? leaf List`: Some(x) ok, None atc (P5, as rc06); every bracket spelling owp (P3c: the List leaf's mark under `?`, R7); braces iop, map notation mna (P3b); x, _, 0 and every record owp (P3c). Paths: R3.
Subject on `? leaf Map`: Some(x) ok, None atc (P5, as rc06); { y -> x, .. } owp (P3c: the Map leaf's mark under `?`); brackets br, braces iop (P3b); x, _, 0 and every record owp (P3c). Paths: R3.

Subject on a List collection: [x, ..], [x] and [x, r @ ..] ok (P3a: the instance list; Q2: a value item is an instance of an ordered collection; P6 rests); [..] ok+no-effect-entry (Q1's lint); [.., x] ok by the principles, the product's ils being the stated limitation (a back instance matched in place, principles #9); braces ils (P2: braces mark unordered instances, on a List collection); Some/None pop, map notation mna (P3b); x, _, 0 and every record cwi (P3c: a value on `*`, B7). Paths: R3.

Subject on a Set or Map collection, the result leaving or writing it alike: { G { a: x, .. }, .. } ok (P3a: one instance record, the other instances framed; on the Map collection it names the key a); every bracket spelling br (P3b: brackets denote nothing on an unordered collection), Some/None pop, map notation mna (P3b); x, _, 0 and every record cwi (P3c on `*`). No entry here constrains nothing, so no lint tells the sides apart. Paths: R3.

As rc01, the result writing the computation: [..] ok without the lint (Q1's lint is for a cell the result leaves out). Some/None pop, braces iop, map mna (P3b); the brackets ok (P3a), [.., x] the product's E1 cbi; [x, r @ ..] cir (Q3); values and records cw (P3c, E2). Paths: R3.
As rc02, the result writing the leaf: _ ok without the lint (Q1). Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x ok; 0 and the records sort (the lattice). Paths: R3.
As rc03, the result writing the leaf: [..] and _ ok without the lint (Q1). Every bracket spelling ok (P3a, P6); braces iop, map mna, Some/None pop (P3b); x ok; 0 and the records sort. Paths: R3.
As rc04, the result writing the leaf: _ ok without the lint (Q1). { y -> x, .. } ok (P3a); brackets br, braces iop, Some/None pop (P3b); x ok; 0 and the records sort. Paths: R3.

As rc05, the result writing the group: _ ok without the lint (Q1). Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x ok; 0 sort; G { a: x, .. } and G { a: x, b: y, .. } ok (P6); G { a: x } rmc (L4). Paths: R3.

As rc06, the result writing the cell: None ok (P5: the result creates it, so K can test its absence). Some(x) ok (P3a); brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); values and records owp (P3c). Paths: R3.
As rc07, the result writing the cell: None ok (P5). Some(x) ok; brackets owp (P3c, R7); braces iop, map mna (P3b); values and records owp (P3c). Paths: R3.
As rc08, the result writing the cell: None ok (P5). Some(x) ok; { y -> x, .. } owp (P3c); brackets br, braces iop (P3b); values and records owp (P3c). Paths: R3.

As rc09, the result writing the collection: [..] ok without the lint (Q1). [x, ..], [x], [x, r @ ..] ok (P3a, Q2, P6); [.., x] ok, the product's ils the stated limitation (principles #9); braces ils (P2); Some/None pop, map mna (P3b); values and records cwi (P3c). Paths: R3.

Result over the computation matched by `[y, ..]`: [x, ..] sort (P6: `..` keeps the subject's rest; x to the lattice); [x] rm (it drops the subject's `..`, D2); [..] ok (it keeps the rest and drops y); [.., x] sort by the principles (it keeps the rest), the product's cbi being E1; [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4 placement: `@` and `_` in a result, F2 and ruling 3, before the kind); Some/None pop, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } cw (P3c, E2; the vacuous `..` leaves nothing open, the R4 ruling); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4: a built record leaving b open, named before P3 (c) because the advice puts it at a term's position). Paths: R3 (alias, wop and the open record are form or kind answers and stand).

Result over a plain Int or Set leaf, matched by the binder `old` or not matched (Q1's overwrite): the same answers, since no rest is paired. Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4 placement, before the kind); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } sort (P5: the new content, its sort to the lattice; the vacuous `..`, R4 ruling); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4: a built term record leaving b open, where Rust reads defaults and K keeps, P0). Paths: R3.

Result over a List or cons leaf matched by `[y, ..]` (P6 at its content root): [x, ..] and [.., x] sort (they keep the rest), [..] ok, [x] rm (it drops the subject's `..`); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } rm (a whole value drops the subject's `..`); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4, at the kind step, before pairing); Some/None pop, braces iop, map mna (P3b). Paths: R3 (rm is pairing, so the ancestor's class replaces it).

Result over a Map leaf matched by `{ z -> y, .. }`: { y -> x, .. } sort by the principles (P6, M3: the frame write keeps the subject's rest), the product's map-read-in-result being the stated limitation (principles #16, #40); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } rm (a whole value drops the subject's `..`); brackets br, braces iop, Some/None pop (P3b); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4). Paths: R3.

Result over the plain group G, matched by `G { a: y, .. }` or overwritten (the same answers: a record's `..` frames children and is no content root, P6): x and 0 sort (P5, the lattice); G { a: x, b: y, .. } sort (the vacuous rest, R4 ruling); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (F3, ruling 1: a bare `..` over an existing group is Rust's defaults, which only a created instance has; pairing, so the ancestor's class replaces it under a path); G { a: x } rmc (L4: a kind refusal, it stands); Some/None pop, brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4). Paths: R3.

Result over `? leaf Int` matched by `Some(old)`: Some(x) sort (P3a, ruling 3), None ok (F1: it removes the matched cell); brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } owp (P3c); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4: the advice `Some(..)` puts it at the leaf's term position, where it is refused again, so it is named first). Paths: R3.

Result over `? leaf List` matched by `Some([y, ..])`: Some(x) rm (ruling 3: inside `Some`, judged by the List kind, where x drops the subject's `..`); None ok (F1); the other bracket spellings owp (P3c: the List mark under `?`); braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } owp (P3c); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4, as rc25). Paths: R3.

Result over `? leaf Map` matched by `Some({ z -> y, .. })`: Some(x) rm (ruling 3: inside `Some`, x drops the map's `..`); None ok (F1); { y -> x, .. } owp (P3c: the Map mark under `?`); brackets br, braces iop (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } owp (P3c); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4). Paths: R3.

Result over `? group G` matched by `Some(G { a: y, .. })`: Some(x) sort (P3a), None ok (F1); brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0 and every record owp (P3c: a value under `?`; the open record's advice `Some(G { a: x, .. })` lands at the group's position, not at a term's, so R4 does not name it first, and F3 refuses it there, deeper); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4). Paths: R3.

Result over a List collection matched by `[G { a: y, .. }, ..]`: [x, ..] sort (Q2: x a front instance; `..` keeps the subject's rest); [x] rm (it drops the subject's `..`); [..] ok (it drops the front instance and keeps the rest); [.., x] sort by the principles, the product's ils being the stated limitation (both ends changed, principles #9); braces ils (P2); Some/None pop, map mna (P3b); x, 0 and every record cwi (P3c on `*`; a record's advice is a created instance, whose bare `..` takes the template's fields, P6); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4). Paths: R3.

Result over a Set or Map collection matched by `{ G { a: y, .. }, .. }`: { G { a: x, .. }, .. } sort (a created instance: its bare `..` is the template's fields, P6; it writes the key a, ruling 3; the set's `..` keeps the subject's other instances); the other bracket spellings br, Some/None pop, map mna (P3b); x, 0 and every record cwi (P3c on `*`); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4). Paths: R3.

Result over the computation the subject does not match (Q1's overwrite): [x, ..], [x], [..] and [.., x] cir (Q3: the overwrite drops the continuation; [.., x] shows the product's E1 cbi, a kind answer); Some/None pop, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } cw (P3c, E2); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4). Paths: R3 (Q3's overwrite is pairing, so the ancestor's class replaces it).

Overwrite of a List or cons leaf (Q1): [x] sort (the exact new list); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } sort (P5: the new content, its sort to the lattice); [x, ..], [..] and [.., x] rm (P6: a `..` the subject never wrote); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4); Some/None pop, braces iop, map mna (P3b). Paths: R3.

Overwrite of a Map leaf (Q1): { y -> x, .. } rm (P6, M3: the frame write keeps a rest the subject never wrote), the product's map-read-in-result being the stated limitation; x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } sort (P5); brackets br, braces iop, Some/None pop (P3b); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4). Paths: R3.

Overwrite of `? leaf Int`: Some(x) and None uor (Q1 x P5: the rule does not know the cell's presence); brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } owp (P3c, the kind before pairing); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4, as rc25). Paths: R3.

Overwrite of `? leaf List`: Some(x) and None uor (Q1 x P5); the other bracket spellings owp (P3c, R7); braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } owp (P3c); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4). Paths: R3.

Overwrite of `? leaf Map`: Some(x) and None uor (Q1 x P5); { y -> x, .. } owp (P3c); brackets br, braces iop (P3b); x, 0, G { a: x, b: y, .. } and G { a: x } owp (P3c); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4); G { a: x, .. } open-record-outside-pattern (R4). Paths: R3.

Overwrite of `? group G`: Some(x) and None uor (Q1 x P5); brackets br, braces iop, map mna (P3b); x, 0 and every record owp (P3c; the records' advice lands at the group's position, as rc28); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4). Paths: R3.

Overwrite of a List collection (Q1): [x] sort (the collection becomes the one instance x, Q2); [x, ..] and [..] rm (P6: a `..` the subject never wrote); [.., x] rm by the principles, the product's ils being the stated limitation (a kind answer); braces ils (P2); Some/None pop, map mna (P3b); x, 0 and every record cwi (P3c); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4). Paths: R3.

Overwrite of a Set or Map collection (Q1): { G { a: x, .. }, .. } rm (P6: the set's `..` keeps instances the subject never matched); the other bracket spellings br, Some/None pop, map mna (P3b); x, 0 and every record cwi (P3c); [x, r @ ..] alias-outside-pattern and _ wop (P4). Paths: R3.

cells! subject on the computation, the result leaving or writing it alike: KCell(x, ..) and KCell(x) sort (P3a: the computation's wrapper; P6's rest; the binder's sort to the lattice); every Cell(..) cw (P3b: a leaf's wrapper, which the stack has nowhere); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b); x, _ and the fragments cw (P3c: a value where `KCell` is the mark). No entry here matches everything and binds nothing, so no lint tells the sides apart. Paths: R3.

cells! subject on a plain Int or Set leaf, either side: Cell(x) sort (P3a: the leaf's wrapper); Cell([x, ..]) br and Cell(k::map![..]) mna (P3b inside the wrapper: no List or Map layer); KCell cw (A: the computation's wrapper, which the leaf has nowhere); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b); x, _ and the fragments cw (P3c: a bare value on a cells! leaf, whose mark is `Cell`). Paths: R3.

cells! subject on a List or cons leaf, either side: Cell(x) and Cell([x, ..]) sort (P3a; P6: the list's rest at its content root); Cell(k::map![..]) mna (P3b inside); KCell cw (A); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b); x, _ and the fragments cw (P3c). Paths: R3.

cells! subject on a Map leaf, either side: Cell(x) and Cell(k::map![y -> x, ..]) sort (P3a: the map read, its rest framed); Cell([x, ..]) br (P3b inside); KCell cw (A); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b); x, _ and the fragments cw (P3c). Paths: R3.

cells! subject on the group G, which has no wrapper (P2): x sort (a whole binder); _ ok+no-effect-entry (R9's lint: it matches all and binds nothing, on a cell the result leaves); the fragments G { a: x, .. } and G { a: x, b: y, .. } sort (P6: a subject's `..`); k::fragment![crate::G { a: x }] rmc (D-4: L4 in both forms, P7; a kind refusal, so it stands under a path); Cell and KCell cw (P3b, A: no layer has a wrapper); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b). Paths: R3.

cells! subject on a `?` leaf (Int, List or Map), the result leaving it: Some(Cell(x)) sort (P3a, then the leaf's wrapper); None atc (P5: K tests absence only by creating the cell); Cell(x), Cell([x, ..]) and Cell(k::map![..]) owp (P3c: the leaf's wrapper under `?`; principles row 20); KCell cw (A: the computation's wrapper, nowhere on the stack); the instance lists iop (P3b); x, _ and the fragments owp (P3c). Paths: R3.

cells! subject on `? group G`, the result leaving it: Some(Cell(x)) cw (P3a, then `Cell` inside, which no group has, P3b: a refusal inside the mark, so it stands under a path); None atc (P5); Cell and KCell cw (P3b, A: no layer of the stack has either wrapper); the instance lists iop (P3b); x, _ and the fragments owp (P3c). Paths: R3.

cells! subject on a List collection, either side: [k::fragment![crate::G { a: x, .. }], ..] sort (P3a: the instance list, P6); its braced form ils (P2: braces mark unordered instances); Some/None pop (P3b); Cell and KCell cw (A: a wrapper of a layer the stack has nowhere, principles row 21); x, _ and the fragments cwi (P3c on `*`). Paths: R3.

cells! subject on a Set or Map collection, either side: { k::fragment![crate::G { a: x, .. }], .. } sort (P3a: one instance record, the others framed; it names the key a); its bracketed form ils (P2: brackets of instance records mark List instances, the collection's instances have another order); Some/None pop (P3b); Cell and KCell cw (A); x, _ and the fragments cwi (P3c). Paths: R3.

As c05, the result writing the group: _ ok without the lint (Q1). x and the open and vacuous fragments sort (P6); k::fragment![crate::G { a: x }] rmc (D-4); Cell and KCell cw (A); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b). Paths: R3.

As c06, the result writing the cell: None ok (P5: the result creates it, so K can test its absence). Some(Cell(x)) sort; Cell(..) owp (P3c); KCell cw (A); the instance lists iop (P3b); x, _ and the fragments owp (P3c). Paths: R3.
As c07, the result writing the cell: None ok (P5). Some(Cell(x)) cw (Cell inside, P3b); Cell and KCell cw (A); the instance lists iop (P3b); x, _ and the fragments owp (P3c). Paths: R3.

cells! result over the computation matched by `KCell(y, ..)`: KCell(x, ..) sort (P6: `..` keeps the rest); KCell(x) rm (it drops the subject's `..`, D2; Q3 binds readable only); Cell(x) and Cell([x, ..]) cw (P3b, A); Cell(k::map![y -> x, ..]) arm (design 2.3's form step: an anonymous rest in a `map!` literal no subject map frames, before the kind); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b); x and the other two fragments cw (P3c); _ wop (P4); k::fragment![crate::G { a: x, .. }] open-record-outside-pattern (R4: the advice `KCell(..)` puts it at a term's position). Paths: R3 (arm, wop and the open record are form or kind answers and stand).

cells! result over a plain Int or Set leaf, matched by `Cell(old)` or overwritten, and over an overwritten Map leaf (no rest is paired, so the answers agree): Cell(x) sort (P5, the lattice); Cell([x, ..]) br (P3b inside: no List layer, the Map leaf's included); Cell(k::map![y -> x, ..]) arm (the form step: no subject map frames it); KCell cw (A); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b); x and the other two fragments cw (P3c: the leaf's `Cell` is missing); _ wop (P4); the open fragment open-record-outside-pattern (R4: the advice `Cell(..)` puts it at a term's position). Paths: R3.

cells! result over a List or cons leaf matched by `Cell([y, ..])`: Cell([x, ..]) sort (P6 keeps the rest); Cell(x) rm (a whole value drops the subject's `..`); Cell(k::map![..]) arm (the form step: no subject map frames it); KCell cw (A); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b); x and the other two fragments cw (P3c); _ wop (P4); the open fragment open-record-outside-pattern (R4). Paths: R3 (rm is pairing).

cells! result over a Map leaf matched by `Cell(k::map![z -> y, ..])`: Cell(k::map![y -> x, ..]) sort (ruling 1 of part (b): the subject's map frames its rest, so the result's `..` keeps it, P6 at the map's content root, M3; P7, as readable's { y -> x, .. } in rc23), the product's arm being the stated M3 limitation, a form-step answer that shows on every line; Cell(x) rm (a whole value drops the subject's `..`); Cell([x, ..]) br (P3b inside); KCell cw (A); Some/None pop, the instance lists iop (P3b); x and the other two fragments cw (P3c); _ wop (P4); the open fragment open-record-outside-pattern (R4). Paths: R3.
